newsitem.title: UK: Euro products outlook - Asian buying to lend suppo.
newsitem.headline: Euro products outlook - Asian buying to lend suppo.

text.p: Sustained demand from the Far East may be the only bright spot this week for a European products market struggling with lacklustre local and transatlantic buying, traders said.

Gasoline is eagerly awaiting the seasonal surge in demand sparked by the U.S. driving season. but while prices started to rise last week on perceptions of fresh transatlantic buying, its failure to appear left the spot market soft with premium unleaded barges valued at $210 a tonne in northern Europe.
Traders see little fundamental demand in Europe to back up the market.
Some supportive hedging activity on the swaps market fizzled out last week.
"(Gasoline) hardly flinched on news of refinery runs cuts this week because of the slack buying, prices could drift lower unless the U.S. window widens," one trader said.
Dealers said some demand could emerge from a Mediterranean markets tightened by refinery maintenance, but freight costs were seen as restrictive to arbitrage elsewhere.
Naphtha needs the seasonal lift of rallying gasoline for fresh upside direction, traders said. Sales to the Far East took out most of the Algerian and Egyptian supplies for March.
But cargoes left attracted little buying interest.
An open arbitrage should continue to draw Russian gas oil eastwards in the wake of the 500,000 tonnes already headed to Asian markets.

Premiums for Russian material are expected to hold steady at April IPE +$2-3 cif NWE, while scarce availabilities should allow German DIN to hold onto sharp gains made last week which took differentials to April +$6/$7 a tonne.
FOD is set to play the poor relative to DIN with sluggish French demand seen unlikely to perk up as spring temperatures kick in.
Differentials are set to hold in the +$2-$4 range despite refinery run cuts crimping supplies.
Heavy fuel is likely to stay flat early this week although some dealers expect renewed downward pressure later.
Tight supply in the Mediterranean and demand into Romania and Singapore will underpin the market before the weight of stored oil in Rotterdam again presses prices lower.

Upwards of 250,000 tonnes of Med fuel has been fixed to head eastwards in March. In the north, high sulphur cracked fuel oil could drift below $80 a tonne fob Rotterdam, last seen 18 months ago when Brent was some $4 below current levels.
Low sulphur cracked fuel was also pressured with healthy supplies in Europe facing competition from U.S. barrels, and traders said levels could slip below 490 a tonne fob.
Despite a weak outlook for prompt fuel oil, prices further forward are buoyant, said traders.

Ship owners bought heavily for the second half of 1997 last week, lifting forward prices and levering the market into even steeper contango, with prompt barges trading some 10 percent below end-year prices.
